diagrams.caption: corbels MCB1
diagrams.represents: Elevation + Section A-A of an in-situ corbel projecting from a column.
diagrams.geometry: Column with corbel cantilevering out; large-radius bend in main tensile bar at column face; two column links near corbel top.
reinforcement: Main tensile reinforcement (large radius bend)
Main tension bars
Secondary horizontal reinforcement (≥0.5× main tensile area)
Compression bars (≥1000mm²/m width, outer bars angled to pass inside links)
Two column links near corbel top
dimensions_labels: Edge distance = bar diameter or 0.75×cover, whichever greater
diagrams.detailing_principle: Illustrates load path: tensile force from bearing travels along main tensile reinforcement, laps in tension into the column; compression strut resisted by compression bars anchored in compression; secondary horizontal reinforcement ties the strut-and-tie mechanism together.
diagrams.applicability_note: Suitable for main tensile reinforcement ≤16mm bar size.

diagrams.caption: corbels MCB2
diagrams.represents: Elevation + Section A-A, same overall arrangement as MCB1 but main tensile bars welded to a cross bar or plate (and to vertical compression bars) instead of relying purely on bent-bar anchorage.
diagrams.geometry: Same as MCB1 but with an explicit weld symbol/callout at the main-tensile-bar-to-cross-bar/plate junction.
reinforcement: Main tensile bars welded to cross bar or plate, and to vertical compression bars
Horizontal links (≥0.5× main tensile area, replacing MCB1's 'secondary horizontal reinforcement' bars)
Compression bars (≥1000mm²/m width)
Two column links near corbel top
dimensions_labels: Edge distance = vertical cover to plate/bar, not less than
diagrams.detailing_principle: Where bar diameter is too large for a practical bend radius (>16mm, up to 20mm here), a welded connection substitutes for the bend — same strut-and-tie logic as MCB1 but with a mechanical (welded) anchorage node.
diagrams.applicability_note: Suitable for main tensile reinforcement ≤20mm bar size.

diagrams.represents: Strut-and-tie schematic showing compression strut and tie, with the critical load-application point flagged.
diagrams.geometry: A compression strut and a tie member meeting at a node; note that the exact position where the load is applied may be critical to the design.
diagrams.detailing_principle: Basis for the general nib design philosophy (strut-and-tie), referenced again in §6.9.2/9.3.1 discussion of shallow nibs and cross-referenced from MN2.
diagrams.cad_reconstructable: Partially — schematic strut/tie lines only, no numeric geometry given.

diagrams.caption: HALF JOINTS MHJ
diagrams.represents: Elevation + Section A-A of a stepped beam end (half joint) bearing detail.
diagrams.geometry: Beam end reduced in depth to form a bearing seat ('h' notation used twice, likely denoting the step height on each side); full-length links; nominal hanger links at 450; nominal links at 150 elsewhere.
reinforcement: Full length links (resist total reaction, equally spaced)
Horizontal U-bar (same diameter as main bottom bars, standard radius bend)
Cranked bars (if necessary, for crack control)
Nominal hanger links at 450
Nominal links at 150
dimensions_labels: Edge distance = bar diameter or 0.75×cover, whichever greater
Tension lap for cranked bar (separate callout)
diagrams.detailing_principle: The half joint transfers a concentrated reaction through the reduced-depth seat; U-bar + hanger links carry the local shear, while full-length links carry the total reaction along the joint. Note this detail is explicitly cross-referenced as ALSO suitable for half joints in slabs (see MN1).
diagrams.supplementary_note: Special design information must be given concerning the bearing pads (out of scope of this manual section).

diagrams.caption: NIBS MN1
diagrams.represents: Elevation + notes for a continuous nib along a beam/wall, general (non-shallow) case.
diagrams.geometry: Nib projecting from a beam/wall face; closed links or U-bars specified by designer to take the nib load.
reinforcement: Closed links or U-bars (designer-specified diameter, max 12mm)
Tension anchorage length (if U-bars used)
dimensions_labels: Edge distance: not less than bar diameter or 0.75×nominal cover, whichever greater
Minimum nominal overlap of reinforcement in nib and supported member = 60
diagrams.detailing_principle: This detail is explicitly noted as ALSO suitable for half joints in slabs, i.e. the same reinforcement logic (vertical link/U-bar carrying load into supporting member, with defined lap overlap into the supported member) applies to both a nib and a slab half joint.

diagrams.member: Continuous nib (shallow, light loads e.g. brickwork)
diagrams.caption: NIBS MN2
diagrams.represents: Elevation + Section A-A of a shallow nib using horizontal U-bars instead of vertical links/U-bars.
diagrams.geometry: Shallow nib, minimum depth 140mm, wired to at least two main longitudinal bars via a lacer bar.
reinforcement: Horizontal U-bars (diameter ≤16mm, pitch ≤250mm)
Lacer bar (same diameter as U-bars, wired to ≥2 main longitudinal bars)
Links (designer-specified, to take load on nib)
dimensions_labels: Depth of nib not less than 140
Pitch of U-bars not more than 250
diagrams.detailing_principle: Used where a shallow nib is required (e.g. supporting brickwork, light loads) and there isn't enough depth for the MN1 vertical-link arrangement; horizontal U-bars substitute, tied together by a lacer bar for stability during construction. Cross-referenced to §6.9.2 strut-and-tie discussion (Fig 6.34).

diagrams.caption: Figure 7.1 Debonding tendons for pretensioned elements / Figure 7.2 Pre-tensioned element with deflected tendons
diagrams.represents: Elevation showing debonded lengths from each end (1700mm and 4500mm examples) and deflected-strand profile; sections A-A/B-B show strand positions (some used, some not, per section).
diagrams.detailing_principle: Debonding length is member-specific and explicitly dimensioned from each end; deflected strands change vertical position along the member length (X m spacing implied by generic 'Xm' labels).
diagrams.cad_reconstructable: Partially — pattern is clear (debonded length as a parameter per strand) but exact numeric profile beyond the two examples is not generalizable without more data.

diagrams.caption: Figure 7.13 Location of bursting reinforcement
diagrams.represents: End elevation + side elevation showing two orthogonal bursting-reinforcement zones (horizontal bursting to depth b, vertical bursting to depth t) relative to the anchorage plate.
diagrams.geometry: t = least dimension of member; zone extends from the anchorage face to depth b (horizontal) or t (vertical); minimum 50mm + 'a' offset from anchor plate edge.
diagrams.detailing_principle: Bursting reinforcement must be positioned within a clearly defined rectangular zone derived from member cross-section and anchor-plate geometry — directly parametrizable (see 10_generator.py `create_end_block_bursting_zone()`).

diagrams.member: Anchorage blister / curved tendon in plan / looped anchorage
diagrams.caption: Figures 7.19-7.21
diagrams.represents: Force diagrams (not primarily detailing geometry) showing radial force components (PR, PV1, PH1, PH2) at blisters, bursting/moment forces around a box girder in plan, and forces at looped anchorages.
diagrams.detailing_principle: These are FORCE/equilibrium diagrams used to justify WHY additional local reinforcement is needed at blisters/curved tendons/loops, not dimensioned reinforcement layout drawings.
diagrams.note: Useful as design-rationale metadata, not as CAD geometry source.

diagrams.caption: 9.4 Typical details — construction & movement joints
diagrams.represents: Three/four joint-section types side by side: (a) construction joint with hydrophilic strip, rebar continuous; (b) movement joint with compressible filler + expansion waterstop, rebar stopped; (c) construction joint with waterstop + crack inducer, rebar continuous.
diagrams.detailing_principle: Waterstop/hydrophilic-strip choice is paired with a rebar-continuity decision (continuous vs stopped) — i.e. each joint TYPE is a fixed bundle of (joint device, rebar treatment, crack inducer presence).
